حَبَّةٌ n. un. of حَبٌّ [q. v.]. (S, Msb, K.) [Hence,] جَابِرُ بْنُ حَبَّةَ a name of (assumed tropical:) Bread. (ISk, S.) ―
-b2- See also حِبَّةٌ, in two places. ―
-b3- [A grain; meaning the weight of a grain of barley;] a wellknown weight. (K.) ―
-b4- A [small] piece, or portion, of a thing. (S, K.) ―
-b5- حَبَّةُ القَلْبِ The heart's core; (AA, TA;) the black, or inner, part of the heart; or i. q. ثَمَرَتُهُ; (S, A, K;) which is that [same thing]: (S:) or a black thing in the heart: (K:) or the black clot of blood that is within the heart: (T, TA:) or the heart's blood. (K.) You say, أَصَابَتْ فُلَانَةُ حَبَّةَ قَلْبِهِ [Such a woman smote his heart's core]. (A, TA.) ＝
-A2- A want: or an object of want; a needful, or requisite, thing: syn. حَاجَةٌ. (K.)
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
